# Arrakis Security raises $8M Seed to secure enterprise AI agents

● 14 days ago

Arrakis Security raises $8M Seed to secure enterprise AI agents

**What's the deal?** Israeli cybersecurity startup Arrakis Security has raised $8 million in Seed funding to build a platform that monitors and governs the behaviour of enterprise AI agents. The round was led by [Hetz Ventures](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/hetz_ventures) , with backing from [ElevenLabs](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/elevenlabs_1) chief executive officer [Mati Staniszewski](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/mati_staniszewski_1) , [Torq](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/torq) chief executive officer [Ofer Smadari](https://app.dealroom.
co/companies/ofer_smadari_2) , Pentera founder and chief executive officer Amitai Ratzon, and several senior Palantir executives.

**Who's behind it?** Founders Tal Baron, Omer Efrat, and Ron Shani are veterans of Torq and Palantir. The company employs around 20 people.

**Why now?** Enterprises are rapidly deploying autonomous AI systems that access sensitive data and execute workflows without human supervision. Arrakis argues that traditional security tools, built for human users interacting with machines, cannot govern software that acts independently.

**What's the endgame?** The platform discovers AI agents across an organisation, builds behavioural profiles, and monitors activity in real time. When it detects suspicious actions — such as data exfiltration or privilege abuse — it can block them, revoke permissions, or suspend integrations. The new funding will expand its research, development, and product teams in Israel.

**What's the pitch?
** Arrakis says companies face a "visibility illusion": they know an agent exists but lack detail on what it is doing and whether it complies with policy. "You cannot secure a machine that thinks and operates differently from humans using security tools that were designed to monitor humans interacting with machines," said Baron.

**The signal:** As agentic AI moves into CRMs, financial data, and internal workflows, a new security layer is forming around non-human identities — shifting the focus from who has access to what autonomous systems actually do once inside.

## Company Overview

### Snapshot

Founded in December 2025, Arrakis Security operates with 1–10 employees. The company secured $8 million in its Seed funding round in August 2026, attracting two investors, with Hetz Ventures identified as a lead investor.

### Business overview

Arrakis Security provides a comprehensive platform for CISOs and security teams, focusing on the discovery, governance, and control of AI agents across SaaS, cloud, and endpoint environments. Its core technology builds behavioral baselines, maps permissions and risks, and enforces policy both pre- and post-execution.
The platform integrates agent observability, AI security posture management, MCP gateway controls, DLP, CVE and framework mapping, runtime anomaly detection, and cross-agent correlation. It serves enterprises and SMBs, enabling visibility and control over non-human identities that access sensitive data and execute autonomous workflows.

### Strategic signal

Arrakis Security's successful $8 million Seed funding round in August 2026, led by Hetz Ventures, signals strong investor confidence in its innovative approach to AI agent security. Arrakis Security is a company, founded in 2026. It raised a $8M Seed in August 2026, from investors including Hetz Ventures.

### About This Round
Arrakis Security , an Israeli company building a security layer for the AI agents running inside enterprises, raised an $8 million seed round announced on 2 August 2026, led by Hetz Ventures . Angels in the round include Mati Staniszewski of ElevenLabs, Ofer Smadari of Torq, Pentera founder Amitai Ratzjon and senior Palantir executives. [1](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/hyklcf2bgg)

The platform starts by discovering which agents are actually operating across an organisation, builds a behavioural profile of each one, then monitors what they do in real time and flags anomalies. When it sees unauthorised access or data leaving where it should not, it can block the action, revoke the agent's permissions or trigger a response workflow. The company was founded by chief executive Tal Baron with Omer Efrat and Ron Shani, all from Torq and Palantir, and employs around 20 people. [1](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/hyklcf2bgg) [2](https://app.dealroom.
co/news/note/arrakis-security-raises-8m-seed-to-secure-enterprise-ai-agents)

Baron frames the problem as a category error in existing tooling: "You cannot secure a machine that thinks and operates differently from humans using security tools that were designed to monitor humans interacting with machines." The company calls the underlying condition a visibility illusion - organisations believing they know what their autonomous systems do. [1](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/hyklcf2bgg)

Discovery is the load-bearing feature here, and it is worth separating from the monitoring pitch that sits on top of it. Enterprise agents do not arrive through procurement; they accumulate, because any employee with an API key and a sanctioned copilot can stand one up, and it inherits that employee's permissions without inheriting the review that granted them.
That makes the first honest answer to "how many agents are running here" almost always wrong, and a security product that can only monitor what it was pointed at is useless against a population nobody has enumerated. The angel list reinforces the read - Torq and Pentera both sell into security operations, and Palantir people know what deployed autonomy looks like inside a large institution. The open question is durability rather than need: identity providers and the cloud platforms are the natural owners of agent permissions, and every capability Arrakis ships is one those vendors could fold into a control plane they already sell. Being early and specific is the whole defence.
